what: Toll Brothers builds luxury houses in the United States, typically larger and more expensive than the national builders, with buyers choosing finishes and options.
customers: Move-up and affluent buyers, and empty nesters, in about two dozen states.
money: houses built to order and speculative inventory
Land sales, joint ventures and financial services
apartments, land development and mortgage services
moat: A luxury brand in homebuilding, which few competitors have, and buyers who are wealthier and less dependent on mortgage rates than first-time buyers.
risks: Luxury demand softens quickly if share prices or bonuses fall
Builds to order, so a cancellation after months of construction is costly
Housing is cyclical and interest rates set the cycle
opportunities: 11.4 times earnings with $1.3B of cash against $1.9B of debt
A 12.3% net margin, among the best in homebuilding, because option upgrades carry high margins
Analysts see about 19% upside, with 18 covering the stock
watch: Net signed contracts and the average selling price, which shows whether buyers are trading down.
